ENG_031.context: After the underlay was updated, some model elements shifted in coordinates.
ENG_031.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the control points and register the shift before the next publication.
options.B: I will compare the coordinate transformation with the source system and register the result of checking the underlay.
options.C: I will compare the base points and control elements before and after the update.
options.D: I will block the release and open a task to check the coordinates.

ENG_032.context: The design load in the calculation report differs from the value in the model.
ENG_032.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check where the two loads come from and personally propose to those responsible a procedure for clarifying the value.
options.B: I will check the source of the load, the calculation date and the model revisions.
options.C: I will tell the adjacent disciplines that the value needs to be clarified and give a deadline for the answer.
options.D: I will check the calculation against the model and give the adjacent disciplines a confirmed value.

ENG_033.context: The model check revealed a fire resistance parameter that is systematically left blank.
ENG_033.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will find out in which template and at what stage the parameter gets lost.
options.B: I will help the discipline authors fill in the parameter and check the standard objects.
options.C: I will find the source of the omissions and agree a mandatory check with the authors.
options.D: I will collect the reasons for the omissions together with the authors and check at what stage the fire resistance parameter should be entered.

ENG_034.context: An adjacent discipline asks you to set the status «approved» on a model that has not been reviewed.
ENG_034.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will keep the review status and go through the checklist according to the regulations.
options.B: I will point out the open checks and change the status after they have been documented.
options.C: I will clarify the scope of the remaining review myself and set the conditions for changing the model status.
options.D: I will explain which checks have not yet been done and when I will carry them out.

ENG_035.context: At a coordination meeting there is an argument about who should redo an opening in the slab.
ENG_035.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will show the source requirements and help allocate the actions for the detail.
options.B: I will propose my own way of allocating the task and clarify the boundaries of the change with the section authors.
options.C: I will propose a clear area of responsibility based on the brief and the model.
options.D: I will give the two disciplines a common view of the detail for a joint decision.

ENG_036.context: One of the model authors cannot see a remark linked to an old revision.
ENG_036.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will agree a new link for the remark with the author and keep the connection to the original entry.
options.B: I will check the element ID and the link between the remark and the revision history.
options.C: I will contact the author and help move the remark to the current object.
options.D: I will check the element's history and update the task link together with the author.

ENG_037.context: The schedule automatically counted elements from the temporary demolition model.
ENG_037.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the category filter and the contents of the source model.
options.B: I will stop the publication and record the schedule set-up error.
options.C: I will identify the extra source, fix the filter and arrange a repeat check.
options.D: I will check the counting filters by phase and issue a corrected version of the schedule.

ENG_038.context: On the drawing, the shaft's dimension to the grid does not match the coordination dimension in the model.
ENG_038.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will name the specific dimension that must not be passed on to the site.
options.B: I will check the model against the sheet and request a corrected release, giving my reasons.
options.C: I will compare the shaft's position with the source dimensions and personally present a way to resolve the discrepancy.
options.D: I will check the grid lines, the dimension chains and the publication date of the view.

ENG_039.context: Contractors often ask the same questions about how embedded parts are designated.
ENG_039.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the recurring queries and add an agreed explanation.
options.B: I will collect examples of unclear designations together with the builders and check what information is missing on the sheet.
options.C: I will compare the queries and find the unclear spot on the standard sheet.
options.D: I will discuss with the site which view of the detail would help when reading the drawing.

ENG_040.context: Before the model is published, a link to an unchecked external file has been found.
ENG_040.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will personally arrange a check of the external link and confirm the set of files for publication.
options.B: I will report that the status of the linked file does not allow it to be included in the release.
options.C: I will check where the link came from and carry out the file approval procedure.
options.D: I will record the problem and publish the model after the link has been checked.

ENG_041.context: A young designer is unsure how to formalise a change after a request from the site.
ENG_041.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will explain which decisions require confirmation from the design author.
options.B: I will go through the request route with him and help prepare the package.
options.C: I will set out the limits of authority and prepare the change request together with him.
options.D: I will suggest preparing the first request with the designer and take responsibility for reviewing the disputed decisions.

ENG_042.context: Publications of several sections with shared links are scheduled for this week.
ENG_042.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will gather the section authors to synchronise the update dates.
options.B: I will check the dependencies, agree a publication window and send out the plan.
options.C: I will agree the order of publications with the authors and record the versions of the shared links for each release.
options.D: I will record the control revisions and dependencies before publication.

ENG_043.context: The site reports that the coordinate of an opening on the sheet differs from the model.
ENG_043.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the references and formalise a correction or a confirmation of the sheet.
options.B: I will compare the history of the sheet and the model and record the confirmed position of the opening.
options.C: I will check the coordinate systems, the reference to the grid lines and the sheet revisions.
options.D: I will log a remark and suspend use of the disputed coordinate.

ENG_044.context: During the facade check, an element's height was found not to match the approved detail.
ENG_044.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check how the height differs from the detail and propose to the responsible person myself a procedure for fixing it before release.
options.B: I will check the family parameter and the constraints in the approved detail.
options.C: I will point the author to the exact place of the mismatch and the confirmation required.
options.D: I will check the parameter against the detail and return the element for correction with justification.

ENG_045.context: The clash report contains dozens of false positives for permissible intersections.
ENG_045.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will classify the hits by cause and check the filter rules.
options.B: I will agree exceptions with the disciplines so that only real conflicts remain.
options.C: I will analyse the causes of the false positives and update the checking rules together.
options.D: I will collect examples of permissible intersections together with the authors and clarify the basis for the checking filters.

ENG_046.context: The release sheet shows a revision index that is not in the change log.
ENG_046.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the sheet against the log and start a correction according to the procedure.
options.B: I will point out the discrepancy and release after the correction has been documented.
options.C: I will personally arrange a check of the release index and record the confirmed revision in the log.
options.D: I will tell the person issuing the release directly about the unapproved index.

ENG_047.context: At a meeting the client asks you to confirm right away that a new opening is technically feasible.
ENG_047.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will state the conditions and arrange a check with the structural engineer.
options.B: I will propose to the client a procedure for checking the opening and agree a response date with the structural engineer.
options.C: I will say which calculations and approvals are needed before confirmation.
options.D: I will involve the structural engineer and organise a check of the proposal.

ENG_048.context: After the BIM template was changed, part of the team continues to use the old set of parameters.
ENG_048.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will agree with the authors on switching to the new template and make parameter checks part of publication.
options.B: I will check the differences between the templates and make a list of mandatory parameters.
options.C: I will hold a short set-up session with the authors and collect questions.
options.D: I will publish a verified list of changes and help the authors update.

ENG_049.context: Before setting out the columns, a discrepancy in grid line coordinates was found on two sheets of the same revision.
ENG_049.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the coordinates with the base grid and the grid line schedule.
options.B: I will suspend setting out and file a request to confirm the coordinates.
options.C: I will check the grid and register the discrepancy before issuing the points.
options.D: I will compare the source coordinates of the two sheets and register the confirmed basis for setting out.

ENG_050.context: A control point after earthworks differs from its previous position.
ENG_050.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will report that the point cannot be used for now and explain why.
options.B: I will confirm the discrepancy with an independent measurement and demand that the point be re-referenced.
options.C: I will check the position of the point relative to the control network and present the conclusion to the site manager myself.
options.D: I will check the stability of the marker and repeat the measurement from an independent base.

ENG_051.context: Two crews use different designations for height benchmarks.
ENG_051.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the catalogue and update the benchmark diagram together with the crews.
options.B: I will collect the designations together with the crews and check whether they refer to the same benchmarks.
options.C: I will check the coordinates and elevations of the markers against the approved catalogue.
options.D: I will gather the foremen and help them reconcile the designations they use.

ENG_052.context: The supervisor asks you to issue an elevation based on a verbal report without a control measurement.
ENG_052.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will personally arrange a check of the elevation and record the confirmed result before giving it to the supervisor.
options.B: I will explain that the elevation will be issued after verification by measurement with an instrument.
options.C: I will take the measurement and enter the result in the established form.
options.D: I will give a time, carry out a control measurement and hand over the documented elevation.

ENG_053.context: After setting out, old axis marks were found on site that do not match the new ones.
ENG_053.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will mark the valid points and indicate which marks are to be considered invalid.
options.B: I will do a short walk-round with the supervisor and help mark the current axes.
options.C: I will show the confirmed diagram and mark the points together with the supervisor.
options.D: I will suggest checking the valid marks together with the crew and take responsibility for explaining the accepted setting-out reference.

ENG_054.context: The surveyors on site have changed, and some field records have not yet been transferred to the log.
ENG_054.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will go over the points with the new shift and help sort out the unfinished measurements.
options.B: I will bring the log up to date and check the control points together.
options.C: I will agree with the new shift on reconciling the field records and record the unfinished handover items.
options.D: I will check the logs and enter the measurements with links to the source files.

ENG_055.context: After the total station was moved, the resection gave an increased misclosure.
ENG_055.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the stations and settings, then formalise a control calculation.
options.B: I will check the source stations with the senior surveyor and formalise confirmation of the instrument set-up.
options.C: I will check the source stations, the resection geometry and the instrument settings.
options.D: I will stop issuing points and record the misclosure in the field log.

ENG_056.context: The as-built survey showed the retaining wall outside its design position.
ENG_056.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the survey results with the design boundary and personally present the grounds for the remark.
options.B: I will repeat the measurement from a control station and compare it with the design tolerance.
options.C: I will tell those responsible about the measured deviation and the need for a decision.
options.D: I will confirm the deviation with an independent measurement and send the diagram to those responsible.

ENG_057.context: At the end of the week, several as-built surveys have no photographic record linking them to their work section.
ENG_057.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will find out at what stage the link between photos and measurements gets lost.
options.B: I will propose a single file naming scheme to the crews and help apply it.
options.C: I will analyse the source of the gaps and introduce a single storage procedure together.
options.D: I will collect examples of lost links together with the surveyors and determine what data needs to be recorded on site.

ENG_058.context: The contractor asks you to sign the pile field drawing before all piles have been checked.
ENG_058.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will mark the unchecked piles and carry out the prescribed control.
options.B: I will explain the restriction, complete the control and formalise a correct drawing.
options.C: I will personally arrange for the pile check to be completed and set the conditions for issuing the as-built drawing.
options.D: I will say that the drawing can be confirmed only for the points that have been checked.

ENG_059.context: Workers report that one of the control markers on the section has been damaged.
ENG_059.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will report the restriction and jointly arrange to reference the survey to verified control points.
options.B: I will propose a procedure to the crew for restoring the marker and agree access for control measurements together.
options.C: I will make clear that the damaged marker cannot be used as a basis.
options.D: I will contact the supervisor and the team to protect the marker and choose a replacement.

ENG_060.context: On two floors elevations are recorded in different formats, and the crew is getting confused.
ENG_060.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will agree a single elevation format with the supervisors and apply it in the diagrams we issue.
options.B: I will bring the records to a single format and check them against the height datum.
options.C: I will show the crew a single marking sample and help update the signs.
options.D: I will check the elevations and bring the marking up to standard together with the crew.

ENG_061.context: The coordinate file received from the contractor does not specify the coordinate system.
ENG_061.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the control stations and signs of a coordinate transformation.
options.B: I will not load the file into the working project without a confirmed system.
options.C: I will check the file against the stations and file a request for the coordinate system.
options.D: I will compare the file with the control coordinates and register the confirmed system before use.

ENG_062.context: A check of the slab axes showed a difference close to the permissible limit.
ENG_062.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will tell the supervisor about the borderline result and the need for confirmation.
options.B: I will repeat the measurement and present the confirmed value with the tolerance.
options.C: I will check the conditions of the borderline measurement and propose my own method for verifying the result.
options.D: I will assess the method's error and repeat the check from another station.

ENG_063.context: Several sections keep having delays because source elevations are handed over late.
ENG_063.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will analyse the causes and help introduce advance requests by work section.
options.B: I will collect the actual request times together with the supervisors and find the cause of delays in providing reference elevations.
options.C: I will trace the step at which requests are delayed.
options.D: I will agree a calendar of elevation needs with the supervisors in advance.
